jobs.title: Corporate Development Analyst II/III/Sr
jobs.description:
At Williams, we’re powering a cleaner, more connected future — and that starts with you. Here, your work fuels communities, drives innovation, and helps deliver reliable energy the world depends on. Join a Fortune 500 team that invests in your growth, values your contributions, and challenges you to make a lasting impact every day.

As Corporate Development Analyst Sr., you'll lead the evaluation and valuation of prospective investment opportunities in and outside of Williams' existing portfolio. You will work on a team of hard-working problem solvers, bringing solutions to sophisticated business challenges. Dealing effectively with ambiguity, balancing big picture thinking with attention to detail, and anticipating your business partners' needs are keys to success!

Responsibilities/Expectations:
- Manages and leads financial modeling and valuation in the evaluation of mergers, acquisitions, divestments, joint ventures, major capital projects and commercial contracting with the goal of proposing innovative solutions and structures to improve value
- Supports the entirety of the merger and acquisition, capital investment, and commercial negotiation process including strategy, opportunity identification, due diligence, deal structuring, execution, and integration
- Assists in formal deal due diligence by reviewing and analyzing company and investment information
- Assesses the competitive landscape, trends, strategic fit, sources of commonalities and potential risks of an investment
- Presents recommendations and proposals to senior leadership and external parties related to prospective transactions and investments
- Conducts research and analysis regarding new growth opportunities
- Mentors, trains, and develops other team members with a focus on promoting team culture and creating an atmosphere of teamwork and trust
- Other duties as assigned

Education/Years of Experience:

Sr:
- ​ Required: Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, related field and minimum eight (8) years’ related experience
- Preferred: Master's degree and minimum ten (10) years' experience
- Preferred: Experience in energy industry
- Preferred: Experience leading economic valuation modeling for mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and capital projects

III:
- Required: Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, related field and minimum six (6) years’ related experience
- Preferred: Master's degree and minimum eight (8) years' related experience
- Preferred: Experience in energy industry
- Preferred: Experience leading economic valuation modeling for mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and capital projects

II:
- Required: Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, related field and minimum three (3) years’ related experience
- Preferred: Master's degree and minimum five (5) years' related experience
- Preferred: Experience in energy industry
- Preferred: Experience leading economic valuation modeling for mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and capital projects

Other Requirements:
- Demonstrates excellent organizational/interpersonal skills and safety as the utmost priority
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate across all levels of the organization
- Proficient use of Microsoft Office applications
- Ability to utilize Excel models for valuation, including Discounted Cash Flow (DCF), Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), and accretion/dilution
- Strong finance skills with a solid understanding of income statements, balance sheets, and a statement of cash flows
- General understanding of the oil and natural gas industry

jobs.title: Manager, Risk Management & Insurance
jobs.description:
At Williams, we’re powering a cleaner, more connected future, and that starts with you. Here, your work fuels communities, drives innovation, and helps deliver reliable energy the world depends on. Join a Fortune 500 team that invests in your growth, values your contributions, and challenges you to make a lasting impact every day.

The Manager, Risk Management & Insurance is responsible for the renewal and administration of the company's corporate insurance programs, including the collection and analysis of underwriting information, negotiation of coverage terms and conditions, review of quotes, binders, and policies, and ensuring continuity and certainty of coverage prior to policy effective dates. This role provides day-to-day leadership for the Risk Management and Insurance team and is responsible for planning, organizing, leading, and evaluating the work of assigned staff to ensure high-quality service and operational excellence.
In addition, this position supports the financial operations of the department through budgeting, forecasting, premium allocation, premium payments, loss analysis, and reporting activities. This role serves as a key liaison among internal stakeholders, external brokers, underwriters, claims administrators, and legal counsel while helping identify and mitigate risk exposures across the organization. Success in this role requires strong leadership, strategic thinking, insurance expertise, and the ability to develop and mentor team members.

Responsibilities/Expectations:
- Leads the design, negotiation, procurement, renewal, and administration of corporate insurance programs and policies covering Williams, affiliated entities, and applicable joint ventures, including underwriting submissions, presentations, policy placement, and compliance reviews.

- Reviews insurance quotes, binders, policies, audits, and related documentation to ensure accuracy, compliance, and coverage certainty.

- Partners with management and key stakeholders to develop risk management strategies, evaluate company exposures, establish best-in-industry processes, and implement company-wide or business-specific initiatives related to risk management, insurance, and claims.

- Leads the corporate claims function, including oversight of third-party administrators, claim investigations, settlements, litigation management, reporting, and coordination with Legal, Operations, and other stakeholders.

- Collaborates with Legal, Supply Chain, Commercial Services, and business partners to review contracts, indemnification provisions, insurance requirements, and policy language to support effective risk transfer and compliance.

- Supports departmental financial activities, including budgeting, forecasting, premium allocation, premium payments, loss analysis, audits, and management reporting.

- Develops analyses, reports, and presentations for leadership and other stakeholders and supports the ongoing identification and management of company risk exposures and surety programs.

- Leads assigned projects and strategic initiatives while providing day-to-day leadership, coaching, development opportunities, and performance management for assigned staff.

- Periodic travel may be required, including property risk surveys, underwriter meetings, conferences, and other business-related activities.

- Other duties as assigned.

Education/Years of Experience:
- Required: Bachelor's Degree in Risk Management, Insurance, Finance, Business, or related field; a minimum of eight (8) years of progressive experience in risk management and insurance, including a minimum of three (3) years of management and/or supervisory experience in the energy industry.

- Preferred: Master's degree in Risk Management, Insurance, Finance, Business, or related field; a minimum of ten (10) years of progressive experience in risk management and insurance, including a minimum of five (5) years of management and/or supervisory experience in the energy industry.

Other Requirements:
- Demonstrates outstanding organizational, interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills with safety as the utmost priority.

- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications and PC-based business systems, with advanced Excel skills preferred.

- Skilled in negotiation, analytical thinking, strategic problem solving, and developing sound recommendations for complex business and insurance matters.

- Demonstrated ability to build strong cross-functional partnerships and work effectively both independently and within a team environment.

- Experience reviewing contracts, insurance provisions, indemnification language, insurance policies, underwriting submissions, and related risk transfer mechanisms.

- Ability to prepare clear, comprehensive, and analytical reports and presentations for leadership and senior management.

- Preferred: Broad, in-depth understanding of the insurance industry and commercial insurance products, including property/business interruption, commercial general liability, directors and officers liability, builders risk, environmental liability, cyber liability, and related insurance structures.

- Preferred: ARM, CPCU, or other relevant professional insurance designation.

- Preferred: Experience with Oracle or similar financial systems.
